newsitem.title: ITALY: FAO sees food problems in Africa's Great Lakes.
newsitem.headline: FAO sees food problems in Africa's Great Lakes.

text.p: Poor harvests, civil unrest and the movement of refugees have taken their toll on the food supply situation in the Great Lakes region of Africa, the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) said.
FAO said the outlook for food supplies was "precarious" in several countries such as Rwanda, Burundi and Zaire and that "large-scale international assistance will continue to be required in 1997".

The agency, in its January-February Food Outlook, said other countries also faced difficulties such as Uganda, where the displacement of residents due to civil strife in the north of the country had resulted in severe food supply problems.
It said that some 280,000 people in Tanzania also would need food assistance following a poor harvest in 1996.

FAO said that in other parts of eastern Africa, some good main crops had been gathered in 1996, but that there were nevertheless problems in Somalia and in Kenya where the main season output fell and a poor secondary crop is expected.
